tasks.prompt: Order the steps for starting up a fictional wastewater plant after an overnight shutdown.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: whole plant, from log review to normal operation.

cards.label: Inspect screens, pumps, and blowers for readiness
Open the influent isolation gate gradually
Start preliminary and primary units as flow arrives
Start aeration blowers and return sludge pumps for the biological units
Verify flows, tank levels, and effluent quality before settling into normal operation
Review the shift log and check for outstanding alarms
Remove lockout devices by authorized staff and restore power to units

tasks.explanation: Alarms and lockouts are cleared first, equipment is checked before flow is admitted, treatment units start in flow order, and verification confirms the plant is stable.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a planned shutdown of one treatment unit for maintenance.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one unit being isolated while the rest of the plant keeps treating flow.

cards.label: Stop chemical feeds serving only the unit being isolated
Drain and flush the isolated unit
Apply lockout and tagout to the unit equipment
Test the atmosphere and confirm safe conditions if entry is required
Open the unit for maintenance work
Notify the supervisor and affected staff of the planned isolation
Divert influent flow to the remaining units or holding capacity

tasks.explanation: Flow is diverted before the unit is emptied, lockout follows draining, atmospheric testing comes after isolation, and only then is the unit opened for work.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for starting up an empty aeration basin for the first time.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: clean, empty aeration basin with installed diffusers, no mixed liquor yet.

cards.label: Fill the basin with primary effluent until the diffusers are covered
Start the blower at low air output and check for an even bubble pattern
Add seed sludge from an operating unit or a delivered seed source
Begin influent feed at a low rate
Monitor dissolved oxygen and adjust air as the biomass establishes
Inspect the basin, diffusers, and air piping for damage or debris
Close the basin drain valve and open the inlet gate

tasks.explanation: The basin is inspected dry, filled before air is applied so the diffuser pattern can be seen, seeded before regular feed, and monitored as loading begins.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for returning a drained clarifier to service.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: circular clarifier emptied for inspection, drive and scraper repaired.

cards.label: Close the drain valve and confirm the sludge outlet line is open
Inspect the tank, drive, and scraper and remove all tools and debris
Check effluent clarity at the launder before full loading
Start sludge withdrawal on a timed cycle once a blanket begins to form
Start the scraper drive once the tank is filling
Open the inlet gate and begin filling the clarifier slowly

tasks.explanation: Tools are out before filling, the drive starts as water enters, sludge withdrawal waits until a blanket exists, and clarity is confirmed last.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for changing over from a running blower to the standby blower.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: aeration air supply, one duty blower and one standby blower.

cards.label: Start the standby blower and open its discharge to the air header
Confirm the standby blower is ready and its valves are lined up
Check basin dissolved oxygen and log the changeover
Close the discharge isolation valve on the stopped blower
Stop the unloaded blower
Unload the running blower as header pressure stabilizes

tasks.explanation: Air supply is never interrupted: the standby machine is proven on the header before the duty machine is unloaded, stopped, and isolated.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for restarting the plant after a utility power outage.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: power has just been restored after a two hour outage.

cards.label: Restart the influent pumps one at a time
Restart the screens and grit equipment
Restart blowers and return sludge pumps
Check the clarifiers and the disinfection system
Log the outage, the restart times, and any abnormal findings
Confirm power is restored and review the alarm list
Inspect wet well levels and reset tripped equipment

tasks.explanation: Power and alarms are assessed first, pumping is restored before downstream process equipment, and disinfection is verified before the event is documented.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for taking one of two grit channels out of service for cleaning.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: twin grit channels, one stays in service.

cards.label: Close the inlet gate on the channel being removed
Shift all flow to the channel that stays in service
Remove the lockout and refill the channel before returning it to standby
Remove the collected grit and wash the channel down
Apply lockout to the channel rake and drive equipment
Drain the isolated channel back to the wet well

tasks.explanation: Flow is fully on the duty channel before isolation, draining precedes lockout and cleaning, and the channel is only refilled after lockout is cleared.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for placing a newly installed process pump into service.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: new centrifugal pump, installation complete, not yet run on process liquid.

cards.label: Prime the pump casing and open the suction valve fully
Start the pump with the discharge valve partly closed
Open the discharge valve gradually to the normal operating position
Check amps, vibration, seals, and piping for leaks under load
Record the baseline readings in the equipment log
Review the manufacturer instructions and the installation checklist
Check the coupling alignment and confirm correct motor rotation with a bump start

tasks.explanation: Rotation is proven before priming, the pump starts against a partly closed discharge to limit load, and baseline readings are taken only under normal load.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for hand raking a manual bar screen during a shift.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: manually raked coarse screen in the headworks channel.

cards.label: Slow or divert flow in the screen channel using the upstream gate
Put on gloves and eye protection and check the portable gas monitor reading
Restore normal flow through the channel and record the amount removed
Wash down the screen area and the rake
Transfer the screenings into the lined screenings container
Rake screenings from the bottom of the bars upward into the collection tray

tasks.explanation: Protective equipment and gas checking come first, flow is controlled before raking, screenings are contained before washdown, and flow restoration is last.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for starting a mechanical bar screen after maintenance.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: mechanically raked screen with wash water and a screenings compactor.

cards.label: Remove lockout devices and restore power to the screen panel
Inspect the screen, rake, and channel and confirm all tools are removed
Place the screen in automatic mode and verify level based starting
Start the screen drive and observe one full rake cycle
Start the screenings compactor
Open the wash water supply valve

tasks.explanation: The channel is clear before power returns, wash water and the compactor must be ready before screenings are produced, and automatic control is last.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a shift handover between two operators.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: outgoing day shift operator handing over to the night shift operator.

cards.label: List equipment out of service and any active lockouts
Review the shift log and the key process trends together
Both operators sign the handover record
Walk the incoming operator through any critical unit needing attention
Highlight active alarms, pending samples, and expected deliveries
Explain process changes made during the shift and why

tasks.explanation: The log review frames the handover, lockouts and changes are covered before alarms and pending work, and signatures close the transfer of responsibility.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for handling a full container of screenings through to disposal.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: filled screenings container at the headworks.

cards.label: Close and secure the container lid
Drain free liquid from the container back to the screen channel
Wash and return the empty container to the headworks
Arrange pickup by the approved disposal hauler
Record the container weight or volume in the solids log
Move the sealed container to the designated storage area

tasks.explanation: Liquid drains back to the process before the container is sealed, records are made before pickup, and the washed container returns last.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for starting an aerated grit tank.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: aerated grit tank with air blowers, a grit pump, and a grit classifier.

cards.label: Start the air blower at a low setting
Open the tank inlet gate and admit flow
Check that the discharged grit looks clean and low in organics
Direct pumped grit to the classifier
Start the grit pump on its timed cycle
Adjust the air until a gentle rolling motion carries organics forward while grit settles

tasks.explanation: Flow and air establish the rolling pattern before grit is pumped, and the quality of the washed grit is the final check.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for running and then shutting down a grit classifier.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: screw type grit classifier receiving pumped grit slurry.

cards.label: Start the grit pump feeding slurry to the classifier
Adjust wash water so grit discharges damp and organics return with the overflow
Stop the grit pump when the grit sump is emptied
Stop the screw after the last grit has cleared the trough
Close the wash water supply
Open the classifier wash water supply
Start the classifier screw drive

tasks.explanation: Wash water and the screw run before slurry arrives so grit never packs the trough, and shutdown reverses the order so the screw clears before it stops.

tasks.prompt: Order the operator response as flow through the screens rises sharply in a storm.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: mechanical screen plus a manual bypass screen, flows still rising.

cards.label: Switch the mechanical screen to continuous high cycle operation
Watch the rising channel level trend on the control screen
Log the peak level and the actions taken once flow recedes
Notify the supervisor if the level approaches the bypass weir
Empty screenings containers before they can overflow
Rake the manual bypass screen to keep it ready

tasks.explanation: Faster screening comes before container management, escalation happens before any bypass, and logging closes the event after flows fall.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for checking horizontal velocity in a grit channel.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: rectangular grit channel, target velocity near 0.3 m/s to settle grit and pass organics.

cards.label: Measure the water depth and the channel width
Record the current plant flow from the influent meter
Adjust the channel gate or flow split and note the change in the log
Compare the result with the target velocity for grit settling
Calculate velocity as flow divided by cross sectional area
Calculate the wetted cross sectional area

tasks.explanation: Velocity cannot be calculated until flow and area are known, comparison follows the calculation, and adjustment is the final step.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a routine inspection of a vortex grit separator.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: vortex grit tank in normal service, inspection from the deck only.

cards.label: Observe the paddle rotation and the surface swirl pattern
Check the drive motor and gearbox for noise, heat, and oil level
Record the findings and any defects in the maintenance log
Flush the grit line with water after sampling
Open the sample port and inspect the pumped grit quality
Check the grit pump cycle by listening for its timed run

tasks.explanation: The inspection follows the equipment from drive to grit discharge, the line is flushed after sampling, and recording is last.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for starting a primary clarifier taken out of service last week.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: empty primary clarifier with a sludge collection drive.

cards.label: Close the drain valve and open the sludge withdrawal line
Inspect the drive, scrapers, and scum skimmer and clear all debris
Check effluent clarity and scum skimming once flow is steady
Set the sludge pump on a timed withdrawal cycle
Start the collector drive as the tank fills
Open the inlet gate and fill the clarifier

tasks.explanation: The tank is inspected empty, filling precedes drive start in this procedure, withdrawal is set once sludge can accumulate, and clarity is checked at steady flow.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for withdrawing sludge from a primary clarifier.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: manual withdrawal through a telescoping valve to the thickener.

cards.label: Line up the withdrawal valves from the clarifier to the thickener
Measure the sludge blanket depth with a core sampler
Record the withdrawal time and the new blanket depth
Close the valve when the draw off turns thin and watery
Watch the sludge at the sample port for density and colour
Open the withdrawal valve slowly and start the draw off

tasks.explanation: Blanket depth decides whether to withdraw, density at the sample port decides when to stop, and the closing blanket check is recorded last.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for clearing scum from a primary clarifier surface.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: clarifier with a rotating scum skimmer and a scum pump.

cards.label: Rotate the skimmer to push scum toward the scum box
Check that the scum baffle is in place and undamaged
Log the scum removal and the pit level
Flush the scum line clear with water
Start the scum pump and empty the scum pit
Flush the scum box with plant water to move solids into the trough

tasks.explanation: Scum must reach the box before flushing helps, the pit is pumped before the line is flushed, and logging finishes the task.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for taking a primary clarifier out of service for the season.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one of three primary clarifiers, the other two remain in service.

cards.label: Close the inlet gate to the clarifier being removed
Shift the flow split so the other clarifiers take the full flow
Wash down the tank and leave it empty and secured
Stop the collector drive and apply lockout
Drain the supernatant back to the plant inlet
Withdraw the accumulated sludge blanket to the thickener

tasks.explanation: Flow leaves first, sludge is removed before draining so it is not stranded, lockout follows the drive stop, and washdown is last.

tasks.prompt: Order an operator daily inspection round on a primary clarifier, following the walkway route.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: routine round, starting at the drive bridge and ending at the outlet end.

cards.label: Check influent distribution and flow split at the inlet well
Check the drive unit for torque alarms, noise, and oil level at the bridge
Adjust the withdrawal cycle based on the blanket reading and record the round
Measure the sludge blanket depth near the outlet end
Check effluent clarity and launder cleanliness at the outlet
Observe the scum skimmer and baffle condition along the surface

tasks.explanation: The round follows the physical route from drive to outlet, the blanket reading drives the withdrawal adjustment, and recording closes the round.

tasks.prompt: Order the response to a primary clarifier sludge blanket found near the surface.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: blanket measured within 0.5 m of the surface, effluent solids rising.

cards.label: Check that the sludge pump and withdrawal line are operating
Confirm the blanket depth with a second core sample
Notify the supervisor and log the event if the blanket still does not fall
Reduce the flow split to this clarifier if the blanket stays high
Recheck the blanket depth after one withdrawal cycle
Increase the withdrawal rate or cycle duration

tasks.explanation: The reading is confirmed before equipment checks, withdrawal is increased before flow is cut, and escalation follows a failed recheck.

tasks.prompt: Order the response for a primary clarifier during a heavy rain flow surge.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: plant flow at twice the dry weather average and still rising.

cards.label: Check scum baffles and skimmers more frequently during the surge
Monitor effluent suspended solids at the clarifier outlet
Restore the normal flow split and withdrawal cycle after the peak passes
Confirm the flow split is even across all clarifiers in service
Increase sludge withdrawal to keep blankets low ahead of the peak

tasks.explanation: Even splitting and low blankets prepare the tanks before the peak arrives, monitoring runs through the surge, and normal settings return only after it passes.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for starting a chemical feed to a primary clarifier for enhanced settling.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: alum feed system, dose already set by the supervisor from jar testing.

cards.label: Check the chemical storage tank level and the feed line condition
Confirm the approved dose and the injection point with the supervisor
Monitor clarifier effluent quality and record the dose and tank level
Verify chemical is reaching the injection point
Set the pump stroke to deliver the approved dose
Start the chemical feed pump

tasks.explanation: Authority and supply come before the pump starts, delivery is verified at the injection point, and effluent response is monitored last.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for seeding a new aeration tank to start activated sludge treatment.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: new aeration tank filled with primary effluent, seed sludge available by tanker.

cards.label: Mix and aerate the seeded contents for several hours without feed
Begin feeding primary effluent at a low rate
Measure dissolved oxygen, pH, and mixed liquor suspended solids
Hold wasting to a minimum while the solids inventory builds
Increase feed gradually as the settleability and clarity improve
Fill the tank with primary effluent and start aeration
Discharge the seed sludge tanker into the aeration tank

tasks.explanation: Seeding follows filling and aeration, a mixing period precedes feeding, measurements guide the ramp up, and wasting is held while inventory builds.

tasks.prompt: Order an operator morning process check routine for an activated sludge plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: start of day shift, plant in normal operation.

cards.label: Measure dissolved oxygen in the aeration basin with a handheld meter
Observe mixed liquor colour and foam on the basin surface
Collect a mixed liquor sample for settleability and solids testing
Adjust air or return sludge settings based on the results
Enter the observations and changes in the process log
Review overnight dissolved oxygen and flow trends on the control system
Check blower operation and air header pressure at the blower room

tasks.explanation: Trends are reviewed before field checks, samples are taken before settings change, and adjustments are made only from the gathered results.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for increasing the return activated sludge rate.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: secondary clarifier blanket rising, supervisor has approved a higher return rate.

cards.label: Confirm the new target return rate as a percent of influent flow
Review the clarifier blanket depth and the mixed liquor solids results
Log the new return rate and the blanket readings
Remeasure the blanket depth before making any further change
Wait and observe the clarifier blanket response
Adjust the return pump speed or valve in one small step

tasks.explanation: Data and the approved target come before the adjustment, one small step is proven by a blanket remeasurement before any further change.

tasks.prompt: Order the response when aeration basin dissolved oxygen falls below the plant target.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: handheld reading of 0.8 mg/L against a target range of 1.5 to 2.5 mg/L.

cards.label: Check blower operation, air valves, and header pressure
Verify the low reading with a second handheld meter or a recalibrated probe
Log the readings, the cause found, and the actions taken
Notify the supervisor and shift flow between basins if oxygen stays low
Check for a load surge by reviewing influent flow and recent discharges
Increase blower output or open air valves to the affected basin

tasks.explanation: The reading is verified before equipment is blamed, air supply is corrected before load shifting, and escalation follows a failed correction.

tasks.prompt: Order the response when aeration basin dissolved oxygen is well above target.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: sustained reading of 4.5 mg/L against a target range of 1.5 to 2.5 mg/L, wasting energy.

cards.label: Reduce blower output in one step
Allow the basin to stabilize and recheck dissolved oxygen
Log the new blower setting and the stabilized oxygen reading
Verify the high reading against the online analyzer trend
Check air valve positions on the basin for a valve left open

tasks.explanation: Verification and a valve check precede the output cut, and the basin must stabilize before the new reading is accepted and logged.

tasks.prompt: Order the response to heavy brown foam building on an aeration basin.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: thick dark brown foam covering much of the basin surface.

cards.label: Check recent wasting records and sludge age information
Observe and describe the foam colour, thickness, and coverage
Record the foam condition and actions in the process log
Monitor the basin over the rest of the shift for foam returning
Adjust the wasting rate as directed by the process control plan
Break the foam down with a water spray from the basin walkway

tasks.explanation: Identification and records come before spraying, wasting changes follow the plan rather than guesswork, and monitoring confirms the result.

tasks.prompt: Order the operator steps when mixed liquor settling deteriorates and the clarifier blanket rises.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: suspected sludge bulking, supervisor to be informed with test results in hand.

cards.label: Run the 30 minute settleability test
Collect a fresh mixed liquor sample from the basin outlet
Report the test results and observations to the supervisor
Increase the return sludge rate to protect the clarifier blanket
Check basin dissolved oxygen for a low oxygen cause
Obtain the mixed liquor solids result and calculate the sludge volume index

tasks.explanation: Samples and index results are gathered before reporting, oxygen is checked as a likely cause, and return rate protects the blanket in the meantime.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for changing a dissolved oxygen setpoint on the control system.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: supervisor has approved raising the basin setpoint from 1.8 to 2.2 mg/L.

cards.label: Confirm the blower output responds to the new setpoint
Watch the dissolved oxygen trend until it settles near the new target
Log the setpoint change, the time, and the reason
Review the recent dissolved oxygen trend with the supervisor
Enter the new setpoint value in the control system

tasks.explanation: Approval and trend review precede the entry, blower response is confirmed, and the change is logged only after the trend settles.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for changing the air intake filter on an aeration blower.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: positive displacement blower with a washable intake filter element.

cards.label: Stop the duty blower and apply lockout to its starter
Place the standby blower in service and confirm air supply is stable
Return the blower to duty or standby as directed and log the work
Remove the lockout and start the blower to test it
Install the cleaned or replacement element and reseat the housing
Remove the intake filter element from its housing

tasks.explanation: Air supply is secured on the standby machine before lockout, the element change happens under lockout, and a test run precedes return to service.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for transferring mixed liquor between two aeration basins to balance solids.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: basin A solids high, basin B solids low, transfer pump available.

cards.label: Line up the transfer pump suction from basin A and discharge to basin B
Measure mixed liquor solids in both basins
Close the transfer valves and log the estimated volume moved
Stop the pump when basin B reaches the target solids or level
Monitor levels in both basins during the transfer
Start the transfer pump at a low rate

tasks.explanation: Both inventories are known before lining up, levels are watched during transfer, and valves close only after the pump stops.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for taking one aeration basin out of service while the plant keeps running.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one of three basins to be drained for diffuser repairs.

cards.label: Close the inlet gate to the basin being removed
Shift influent feed and air supply to the remaining basins
Wash down the empty basin and secure it for the repair crew
Stop the basin air supply and apply lockout to its equipment
Drain the remaining liquid to the plant inlet
Transfer its mixed liquor to the operating basins

tasks.explanation: The remaining basins take the load first, usable mixed liquor is saved by transfer before draining, and lockout precedes washdown.

tasks.prompt: Order the cold weather operating adjustments for an activated sludge plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: sustained cold weather, effluent ammonia beginning to climb.

cards.label: Confirm the higher sludge age target with the supervisor
Review the mixed liquor temperature and ammonia trends
Log the adjustments and the trend results
Recheck ammonia and settleability after the change takes effect
Check heat tracing and insulation on exposed process lines
Reduce the wasting rate in one small step to build solids inventory

tasks.explanation: Trends and an approved sludge age target come before the wasting cut, exposed lines are protected in parallel, and results are verified after.

tasks.prompt: Order the process control steps for checking the food to microorganism ratio.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: weekly process control check using lab results.

cards.label: Obtain the mixed liquor volatile solids result for the aeration basin
Collect the influent flow and BOD results for the period
Adjust wasting or feed split as directed and record the calculation
Compare the ratio with the plant target range
Calculate the food to microorganism ratio from the load and the inventory
Note the aeration basin volume in service

tasks.explanation: Load, inventory, and volume data are all required before the ratio can be calculated, comparison follows, and adjustment is the last step.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for collecting a representative mixed liquor sample.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: grab sample for solids and settleability testing.

cards.label: Fill the container, cap it, and wipe the outside clean
Label the container with location, date, and time
Deliver the sample to the lab promptly and note it in the sample log
Rinse the sample container and dipper with mixed liquor
Collect the sample below the surface at the basin outlet area, away from the foam layer

tasks.explanation: Rinsing prevents dilution error, the sample is taken below the foam for representativeness, and labelling and prompt delivery protect the result.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for starting a trickling filter after a winter shutdown.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: rock media trickling filter with a rotary distributor and recirculation.

cards.label: Open the filter inlet gate
Inspect the distributor arms, nozzles, and underdrains and clear debris
Monitor effluent quality as full feed is established
Check the underdrain outlet for free drainage
Verify the distributor rotates evenly under flow
Start the recirculation pump to wet the media gradually

tasks.explanation: Debris is cleared dry, recirculation wets the media before full feed, rotation and drainage are verified, and effluent quality confirms startup.
